title: Raising a Cancellation Charge Against an Event Services Agreement
content:
Where a client holding a Private Event & Banquet Services agreement has called off a confirmed event, a charge falls due on that booking and is raised against the agreement the booking sits under. What the client's account then carries for that cancelled booking is the amount raised.

## When the charge is fixed

The charge for a cancelled event is not fixed until the event ledger carries, for that booking, a cancellation entry recording the day written notice was given and the contracted event value standing at that day.

Put the other way about: for so long as no such entry stands against that booking in the agreement's event ledger — one carrying the day written notice was given and the contracted event value standing at that day — the charge for that event is not yet a fixed amount.

What is raised is the full charge the cancelled booking carries, and deposit money standing against that booking is set against it when the charge is settled rather than when it is raised.

## How the charge is raised

The tool `post_cancellation_charge_5262dfa3` is unlocked at the desk and then called. One call writes a single cancellation charge entry into the agreement's event ledger, carrying the booking it answers, the day the cancelled event was to have been held, the day written notice was given, the amount charged, and today as the day it was raised; a bill reference is minted for the charge and printed on it. The client sees the charge and its bill reference on the agreement's event ledger.

## The values it is given

| Value | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `banquet_agreement_id` | The reference number of the private event and banquet services agreement the cancelled booking sits under, as the agreement lookup returns it. |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the client organisation profile charged, as the profile lookup returns it. |
| `booking_reference` | The cancelled event booking the charge answers, written as BQ- followed by 6 digits, exactly as it stands on the cancellation entry in the event ledger. |
| `event_date` | The day the cancelled event was to have been held, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the venue's own local calendar, with no time part. |
| `notice_given_date` | The day the client gave written notice of the cancellation, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the venue's own local calendar, with no time part. |
| `cancellation_charge_usd` | The amount charged for the cancelled booking, in USD, to 2 decimal places, rounded to the nearest cent at the moment it is recorded, a half-cent going to the nearer even cent, and never left blank. |

## What comes back

A confirmation line of text naming the charge entry reference minted for the posting, the bill reference the charge sits on, written as INV-BQ- followed by 6 digits, the booking reference charged, the amount raised in USD to two decimal places, and the day it was raised, written as YYYY-MM-DD. The line being returned is what indicates the charge was raised; the entry is then visible on the agreement's event ledger.
